title: First weeks with Henderson: Cotton Club, Lafayette and the Club Alabam
summary: Scott recalls the early engagements, the Palace Theatre ambition, and the quality and arrangements of Henderson's musicians.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now, wasn't this a new Fletcher Henderson band? He was forming a new band. It wasn't a band that you just joined. Didn't he form a band just to go into the Club Alabam?

No, well, I haven't come to that. I joined Fletcher. Well, we met, and he played at the Cotton Club. We played there a couple of weeks. Then we played at the . Then we played at the Lafayette Theatre, because that was the theatre in Harlem. We played at Lafayette Theatre, white people used to come there, too, and agents and things to see you. If you're good, you're booked downtown at the Palace Theatre. That was the big place, the Palace.
Well, they -- we played there, and then Fletcher told us that we were going to open up at 44th Street, off Broadway,

the Club Alabam.
Well, I was sailing on a cloud then. I was with a band, and those guys, they're all such good musicians. And to be able to play with them meant so much to me. I felt so great. Boy. That Coleman Hawkins, he was wonderful, marvelous. And Don Redman, he could play trumpet. He played all the reed instruments, and he played trumpet, too.

But the thing was, Fletcher was an arranger. He arranged all the music we played. We didn't play for the sheets. We played his arrangements. That's the thing that put his band -- made it a little different from the other bands, because they played from their music sheets. -- I.E., stock was.
